service.description: Shippo's rates of the asked methods for the packages given: one Shippo shipment per package, each method's cheapest rate of its service level and carrier account per package, summed for a method rated for every package in one currency. Refuses a package with no weight or box dimensions (PARCEL_INVALID) and an address Shippo rejects (ADDRESS_INVALID).

An order part's Shippo rate for its carrier and method (or those given) and the packages given, and with createOrderItem its shipping item. Refuses no package information (PARCEL_INVALID), no carrier (METHOD_REQUIRED), no rate (METHOD_UNAVAILABLE) and a rate in another currency than the order's (CURRENCY_MISMATCH).
The Shippo rate of a shipment's packages (or one) at the route segment's method or the one given.

actions.script: for (const field of Object.keys(answer)) context[field] = answer[field]

service.description: A label per package (the return label with getReturnLabels): a fresh Shippo shipment, the rate of the method's service level recorded on the package before it is bought synchronously with the request reference in the transaction's metadata. A finished label is filled in (transaction, rate and shipment ids, label format, link and file, tracking number, charge and currency); a QUEUED or WAITING one answers pending and is retrieved later, never bought again; a package whose rate already has a transaction gets that one. Refusals throw their code: CONFIG_INVALID, PARCEL_INVALID, ADDRESS_INVALID, METHOD_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_EXPIRED, LABEL_REFUSED, RATE_LIMITED, RATES_NO_ANSWER (nothing bought); a purchase with no answer throws CARRIER_TIMEOUT and a status not understood CARRIER_NO_ANSWER, lost answers find#ShippingLabels resolves. With several packages each one is on its own, and a lost answer or a pending package is thrown before a refusal.

What Shippo did for a request whose answer was lost or pending: the transaction with the request's metadata (by the package's rate, then the transactions created since the request), filled in when finished, pending while QUEUED or WAITING or while a lost request is younger than the lookup grace; for a refund request the package's refund or its label's status. Nothing is bought.

actions.script: for (const field of Object.keys(answer)) context[field] = answer[field]

service.description: Each labelled package's refund: SUCCESS sets gatewayRefundStatus refunded; QUEUED or PENDING keeps the refund id with no status and answers pending (find#ShippingLabels reads it later); a refused refund is REFUND_REFUSED unless the label's transaction is already refunded; NO_LABEL when no package has a Shippo label.

Each labelled package's tracking status, estimate and tracking number from its Shippo transaction (outbound and return labels), and a label file not downloaded yet; a package that fails is logged and the others go on.

Shippo's validation of the address: its trust level (CmtlValid, CmtlInvalid, CmtlIncomplete), the validation messages and Shippo's address id. A provider failure is a warning and leaves the address as it was.

The receive service of ShippoWebhook. The endpoint /rest/sm/ShippoWebhook/{remote} checked the remote's Shippo-Auth-Signature (SmatHmacSha256Timestamp) or URL token (SmatUrlToken) against its sharedSecret; a remote with neither is refused (WEBHOOK_UNAUTHENTICATED). The event is kept once per remote and body (store#ReceivedSystemMessage), so a repeated delivery answers success and is not consumed again.

parameter.name: duplicateOfId
parameter.description: The message already kept for this event

service.description: The consume service of ShippoWebhook: the packages a transaction or tracking event is about, among the shipments of the Shippo gateways on the message's remote. A package with a request still without an answer has it finished through find#ShippingLabels (WarehouseTaskServices.finish#PendingLabelRequests), never bought again; any other is tracked from its Shippo transaction. The payload's status is never applied as it is, so repeated, late and out-of-order events converge; a test event on a production remote is ignored.
